name: Tempus AI
verdict_line: Real data-network moat, but priced as software when three-quarters is a reimbursement-gated lab — demanding until the 73%-GM data leg compounds (NRR back above 100%) and GAAP FCF beats dilution.

name: Caris Life Sciences
verdict_line: Profitable precision-onco lab (+79%, 65% GM, +$442m net cash) at a Dx-not-software ~5x EV/sales; good business fairly-to-cheaply priced, but the re-rate hinges on one ASP reset holding.

name: Natera
verdict_line: Category-leading tumor-informed MRD franchise with a rising ~65% GM and a landed cash inflection, but priced full — the ~15x-sales multiple already assumes the uncontracted Signatera ASP climb to $2,000 and durable CMS coverage both hold, and the coverage/evidence moat (~5-8yr) is capped by budget-neutrality repricing risk.

name: Guardant Health
verdict_line: Good business, richly expected: genuine liquid-biopsy franchise with a real coverage moat, priced at a software-annuity multiple its per-test margins and reimbursement-gated screening TAM have not yet earned.

name: Exact Sciences
verdict_line: Good business: real code/coverage screening moat plus rare positive FCF, acquired by Abbott at a full but defensible ~7x-sales expectation — the franchise, not the AI, got paid for.

name: Personalis
verdict_line: Differentiated MRD tech in a capital-hungry, reimbursement-gated per-test archetype, priced rich (~15x EV/sales) as if the coverage-and-margin crossover is already won when the margin line says it has not begun.

name: Veracyte
verdict_line: Good business — GAAP-profitable, self-funding, ~76% GM, coverage-moated core — at a full-to-rich expectation that already banks an MRD re-acceleration the guide does not show.

name: GE HealthCare
verdict_line: Durable #2 imaging OEM with installed-base lock-in, priced as a low-growth industrial at ~12-13x forward P/E; good business at a fair-to-cheap expectation, but the AI moat is refuted.

name: Butterfly Network
verdict_line: Real, hard-to-copy ultrasound-on-chip (a semiconductor moat, not a healthcare-AI one) bolted to an unproven, one-deal-deep Embedded licensing story, priced at ~16x forward EV/sales as if the platform is already built — good technology, rich expectation.

name: Absci
verdict_line: A real, well-funded AI-antibody call option — not a good business yet, priced on an analyst-assumed 35% coin-flip on one POC, with a data-flywheel moat that is refuted and untested by the flagship.

name: Recursion
verdict_line: Capital-hungry pre-revenue own-pipeline book; the data flywheel is the sub-sector's clearest refutation, and ~30x milestone-lumpy sales still capitalizes an unproven flywheel-to-drug link.

name: Schrodinger
verdict_line: Good capital-light software moat (~5-8yr) strapped to a de-risked option-value pipeline, priced full on a re-acceleration the last prints (11% growth, 81%->69% GM) haven't earned; net cash is the floor.

name: CRISPR Therapeutics
verdict_line: Strongest survivor of a hard owned-pipeline gene-editing cohort — approved product, ~$2.0bn cash, correctly liver/blood-concentrated pipeline — but ~$2.7bn EV prices in-vivo Phase-II success and a >$1bn Casgevy peak the readouts have not yet earned; a good balance sheet at a full expectation.

name: Beam Therapeutics
verdict_line: Cohort leader with the best AATD human dataset and funding to mid-2029, at a fair-to-slightly-rich binary-option price; good asset optionality, not yet a good business.

name: Intellia
verdict_line: Cohort's clearest clinical winner (first in-vivo Ph3 win), but priced at a full expectation that has already banked lonvo-z approval and pays up-front for a ramp and ATTR share facing unpriced friction.

name: Prime Medicine
verdict_line: Distressed tail of the editing cohort: pre-revenue, cash into 2027 racing 2027 readouts, priced ~$570m EV as a survival option not a franchise.

name: Generate Biomedicines
verdict_line: Single-asset Phase-3 binary priced with a platform-moat premium the audit refutes; expectation looks full ahead of the SOLAIRIA readout that decides everything.

name: Insilico Medicine
verdict_line: Commoditizing AI drug-discovery platform wrapped around one differentiated binary asset (rentosertib) — real human POC, priced at a rich ~50x-shrinking-sales pipeline-optionality expectation, not a franchise.

name: NVIDIA
verdict_line: Exceptional infra-toll (~75% GM, ~45% FCF margin, CUDA moat) at a fair-to-full expectation; ~30x trailing holds only if margins and capex cycle persist — own as the semis/AI toll, not a healthcare name.

name: Microsoft
verdict_line: Good business at a fair-to-full expectation, but NOT a healthcare-AI expression: Dragon Copilot is a durable infra-toll fragment inside an AI-capex bet, immaterial to the multiple.

name: Alphabet
verdict_line: Durable L0 platform (decade+ moat, 31.6% margins) at a fair ~27x market multiple, mid-transition to capital-hungry as capex doubles to ~$180bn; healthcare-AI content is free optionality, not a thesis.

name: Amazon
verdict_line: Durable L0 compute toll (AWS) at a full expectation; risk has shifted from growth to whether the $200bn AI build earns its cost of capital before depreciation compresses the 37.7% margin — the One Medical/HealthScribe healthcare angle is a strategic wedge, not a value driver.

name: Oracle Health / Cerner
verdict_line: Durable #2 EHR rail with a real L0 switching-cost moat, but a ~9%-revenue, share-losing, margin-dilutive annuity inside a stock priced entirely on AI-cloud — good business at a fair-to-full expectation, not the reason to own or avoid ORCL.

name: Waystar
verdict_line: Profitable, capital-light owner of the payer claims-to-cash rail — good business at a fair-to-slightly-cheap expectation if ~112% NRR holds against Epic envelopment.

name: Doximity
verdict_line: Good business (>90% GM, net-cash, ~49% FCF-conversion, verified-physician audience moat) but mis-archetyped as SaaS when it is ad-cyclical, at a fair expectation that still embeds a re-acceleration the FY27 ~+4% guide does not support.

name: Veeva Systems
verdict_line: Best-in-study durable owned-workflow / data-licensing compounder — GAAP-profitable, net-cash, ~45% non-GAAP margins, >100% cash conversion — now at a full expectation that prices durability over growth as a finite vertical decelerates to ~12%.

name: Isomorphic Labs
verdict_line: Demo-plus frontier drug lab; the only credible moat (owned assets vs risk-bearing pharma) is real but binary and unproven, gated on a ~40% Phase II wall no lab has moved — size for optionality, not conviction.

name: Xaira Therapeutics
verdict_line: Well-capitalized frontier shot on goal, but demo/optionality not durable value capture: data flywheel is the refuted discovery form, own-pipeline moat gated by the ~40% Phase-II wall with zero human data; priced at a thin ~2.7x on capital.

name: Iambic Therapeutics
verdict_line: Demo/optionality: a fast AI discovery platform (~1-year commoditizing moat) wrapped around one early-stage owned HER2 asset gated by an unproven Phase-II efficacy readout.

name: Genesis Therapeutics
verdict_line: FEATURE-PLUS, not yet a durable value-capturer — grade C+ (conditional), confidence MEDIUM: commercially validated platform whose model commoditizes in ~1yr and whose value sits behind the unmoved ~40% Phase-II wall.

name: Retro Biosciences
verdict_line: Demo/optionality pre-clinical longevity bet, not a durable value-capturer — full expectation on the Altman/OpenAI narrative, with the headline AI edge rented from OpenAI and everything gated on the unchanged ~40% Phase-II wall.

name: Chai Discovery
verdict_line: Best-in-class founders and real pharma access on a commoditizing model layer (its own Chai-1 is the proof); demo/feature with relationship optionality, not yet a durable value-capturer, at a rich private mark — Grade C+.

name: EvolutionaryScale
verdict_line: World-class protein-AI science on a commoditizing model layer with no owned asset, payment rail, or data-attach moat; standalone company effectively ended ~18mo post-seed in a CZI acqui-hire.

name: OpenAI (life sciences)
verdict_line: Durable general-infrastructure toll (L9x, ~5-10yr) wearing a biology skin — but a demo, not a moat, in drug discovery; bio value accrues to the API toll and partner equity, not an owned asset.

name: Anthropic — Claude for Life Sciences
verdict_line: Durable compute toll at the parent level wearing a life-sciences costume — good business, but healthcare-AI expectation priced onto a frontier-model multiple.

name: Latent Labs
verdict_line: Credible AlphaFold-alumni team and a real lab-validated benchmark, but sitting on the L9b model-IP layer Ch5 dates at ~12 months; picks-and-shovels positioning is right, monetisation unproven, durable moat unbuilt — watch, don't own.

name: Abridge
verdict_line: Conditional durable value-capturer (B-): ~30%-share ambient-scribe leader, capital-light but a feature-not-franchise until the coding/CDI/RCM + licensed-CDS up-stack converts to owned workflow that survives Epic envelopment at price; rich ~50x-ARR pre-envelopment venture mark.

name: Ambience Healthcare
verdict_line: Conditional value-capturer: scribe leg is a rented slot, coding/CDI attach is the durable-shaped survivor — real but unproven at price and under-capitalized vs Epic and Abridge, at a rich ~40x mark. Grade C+, medium confidence.

name: Suki
verdict_line: Credible ambient-scribe with the right platform bet, but a feature sandwiched between a commoditizing LLM and the EHRs — no durable moat banked at a ~$0.4–0.5bn mark.

name: Commure (+Athelas)
verdict_line: Conditional value-capturer: L8 claims-to-cash rail is a durable moat candidate, L6 scribe already enveloped by Epic — insider-marked, subsidy-flattered roll-up at a full expectation. C+ / speculative.

name: Cohere Health
verdict_line: Conditional durable L8 utilization-management rail on the right side of the moat map, but pricing power is asserted (ARR growth) not proven (NRR-at-price); grade B / B-, full expectation.

name: Anterior
verdict_line: Durable value-capturer, EMERGING — right side of the workflow-ownership moat, but retention-at-price is unproven for a private at this stage.

name: OpenEvidence
verdict_line: Conditional durable value-capturer (B/B-plus): real revenue and 40%-physician distribution with a licensed-corpus + habit moat that clears the scarce-input bar, but the input is rented and the model commoditizes, so at ~80x run-rate the ~$12bn mark already prices near-perfect execution.

name: Hippocratic AI
verdict_line: Category-leading patient-facing voice AI whose only durable moat candidate — the accumulated safety record — is real but unproven on retention-at-price, at a full $3.5bn mark on no disclosed revenue.

name: Aidoc
verdict_line: Conditional value-capturer, demo-until-proven (C+/B-): real distribution and breadth, but the moat lives entirely in whether aiOS becomes owned orchestration vs a commoditizing model on rented rails.

name: Viz.ai
verdict_line: Durable value-capturer, narrowly — grade B/conditional-yes: owns an embedded multi-disease coordination workflow plus a life-sciences data-attach, but the algorithm commoditizes and the NTAP is transitional, not a permanent code.

name: Epic Systems
verdict_line: Durable decade-plus platform moat — the EHR system-of-record every L6 scribe rents from — but structurally un-investable: no equity, no external capital, private by design.

name: Ever Fortune AI
verdict_line: Best listed TW healthcare-AI pure-play — real loss-to-profit turn, broadest SaMD licence book — but small, ~12% GM, no NHI code, no investable moat, priced ~17x sales on a milestone-gated tech-transfer.

name: aetherAI (雲象科技)
verdict_line: Differentiated TW pathology-workflow pure-play with a thin-but-real installed-base moat that routes around the NHI chokepoint, but a loss-making micro-cap whose equity case rests on an unproven US/EU export push against global incumbents.

name: Acer Medical
verdict_line: Genuine first-mover imaging-triage SaMD with a strong parent, stranded one value-chain layer short of the payment dollar; real-but-not-investable moat and a domestic thesis gated on an NHI reimbursement vote that has not fired, at a rich brand-and-optionality expectation.

name: Amcad Biomed
verdict_line: World-first ultrasound-CAD franchise but a shrinking NT$30m-revenue micro-cap with no company-captured moat — a positioning marker gated on one binary NHI vote, not an investable long.

name: EBM Technologies
verdict_line: Watch-only: a sticky but mature, ex-growth domestic PACS incumbent whose imaging-AI aggregation-rail re-rate is plausible but unproven, undisclosed, and contested — a conditionally good business at a full expectation.

name: Health2Sync
verdict_line: Real, differentiated TW chronic-disease DTx/data-platform with genuine ~69% software margins and a growing Japan-export line, but pre-profit, richly/softly priced on 興櫃 (~140-170x sales), hinging on a single unproven 2026 NHI vote; the 1.6M-user data moat is a scale story, not a defensibility story — pharma/Japan-enterprise relationships are the only sticky leg.

name: ASUS AICS
verdict_line: Genuine L7-L8 coding/HIS node with a >NT$10bn parent-funded push, but zero standalone economics inside a NT$180bn/quarter PC-server parent, a state-captured (not company-captured) data moat, and a dead export proof point — not underwriteable as a healthcare-AI position.

name: Quanta QOCA
verdict_line: Largest-coverage TW medical cloud, but undisclosed, immaterial, and founder-declared non-commercial inside a NT$2.1tn AI-server ODM — a positioning marker, not an investable healthcare-AI pure-play.

name: Wistron Medical
verdict_line: Real dialysis-AI business but structurally uncapturable by an equity holder — unlisted, undisclosed, NHI-gated; only vehicle (3231) is an AI-server bet, not a healthcare-AI one.

name: Foxconn Health / CoDoctor (鴻海醫療, 2317 TT)
verdict_line: Positioning marker, not an investable healthcare-AI pure-play: real deployments (7 medical centres, TFDA-cleared devices, ~US$1.5bn "Healthy Taiwan" integrator role) but zero disclosed health economics, no standing NHI payment, and a moat that belongs to the ~NT$3.4tn ICT parent, not the health unit.

name: Taiwan hospital AI centres
verdict_line: Structural node, not a security — a real, deep, two-sided moat that is state-captured and stranded on non-listed balance sheets; use as the lens for pricing vendors selling INTO it, never as an exposure.

name: Eli Lilly
verdict_line: The mega-cap incumbent that funds AI drug discovery and keeps the value; AI is a cheap option and efficiency lever, immaterial to a ~$1.15tn valuation built on the GLP-1 franchise, not AI.

name: Merck & Co
verdict_line: Good, durable pharma franchise but the whole equity thesis is Keytruda-cliff succession, not AI; the cleanest incumbent example of the study's core claim - MRK funds the AI (Variational, Mayo, internal GenAI) and keeps the value because it, not the vendor, bears the clinical risk and owns distribution. AI is a cost-side hedge, never the moat; expectation reads full because the 2028 cliff is priced as more solved than it is.

name: Pfizer
verdict_line: The cleanest incumbent case: Pfizer rents commoditizing AI models from the frontier labs, embeds them as an opex cost lever inside a $10-11bn R&D line, and keeps all the value at L9 because it owns the reimbursed molecule, the trial, the approval, the distribution, and the balance sheet the startups lack; a good business priced cheaply (~7% yield) for the patent cliff, not for AI, which does not move the binding Phase II constraint.

name: Johnson & Johnson
verdict_line: Diversified incumbent that funds the AI on BOTH chains - drug discovery (Isomorphic, milestone+royalty, keeps the molecules) and surgery (Ottava/Polyphonic, owns the robot + operating-room data) - and keeps the value; at ~$633bn on $94bn revenue, AI is a cheap two-front option, immaterial to the P&L; the real story is the patent-cliff-exposed pharma franchise and a contested surgical platform vs Intuitive, not algorithms.

name: AbbVie
verdict_line: Diversified immunology incumbent that out-ran the Humira cliff via Skyrizi/Rinvoq and serial M&A; uses AI as a cheap internal tool plus a few option-sized deals (BigHat, Caris/ConcertAI) while keeping every asset - AI is immaterial to the ~$460bn valuation and it invests more cautiously than AI-forward peers.

name: Amgen
verdict_line: Durable diversified biotech that both funds and builds its own AI (owns deCODE data), but keeps value at L9 because it bears Phase-II risk and owns the molecule; equity is a MariTide-obesity and base-durability call, not an AI story, and gets near-zero AI premium.

name: Bristol Myers Squibb
verdict_line: Good business, cheaply priced as a patent-cliff pharma not an AI story; the incumbent funds the AI (insitro >$2bn pact, Claude across 30,000 employees) and keeps the drug at L9, but a steep near-term Eliquis/Opdivo/Revlimid cliff - not AI - governs the stock, and AI does not move Phase II biology or LOE replacement.

name: Novartis
verdict_line: One of the deepest AI adopters in big pharma - four external AI-discovery deals plus the data42 internal platform - and the cleanest European illustration of the study's rule: the incumbent funds the AI as cheap staged options and keeps the drugs, trials, and value. At ~$293bn on ~$54.5bn sales, AI is immaterial to the P&L; the real story is pipeline replacing the largest patent cliff in company history. Good business, wide-but-cliff-sensitive franchise moat (not an AI moat).

name: Roche
verdict_line: The incumbent most like a data platform - already owns Flatiron (outcomes), Foundation Medicine (genomics), and Genentech plus the largest disclosed pharma GPU footprint, but at ~$330bn on CHF 61.5bn revenue it is a pipeline bet, not an AI story; Roche funds the AI, keeps the data and the drugs, and captures the value for well under 1% of R&D.

name: AstraZeneca
verdict_line: Good business, wide franchise/oncology moat - not an AI moat; the incumbent funds the AI, licenses shared oncology models, and now buys the AI outright (Modella) while keeping the drugs, trials, biomarkers, and value. AI is immaterial to the ~$292bn valuation, which is priced on the $80bn-by-2030 pipeline, not AI.

name: GSK
verdict_line: Cash-rich incumbent and early AI-in-discovery mover (23andMe 2018, Cerebras 2022, Noetik virtual-cell subscription 2026) that funds the AI and keeps the drugs; AI is immaterial to a ~32.7bn-pound company whose real story is a 2028-29 HIV patent cliff vs pipeline plus M&A backfill. Priced for the cliff, not for AI.

name: Sanofi
verdict_line: Loudest "all in on AI" incumbent - 20,000-user internal plai tool plus 5+ external AI-discovery deals - but AI is immaterial to a ~$103bn cap; the real story is Dupixent concentration (~36% of sales) versus the coming patent cliff, with AI a cheap staged-option efficiency bet the incumbent funds while keeping the drugs, trials, and value.

name: Novo Nordisk
verdict_line: GLP-1 mega-cap incumbent that funds AI (Valo milestones), rents its compute (Gefion, owned by its Foundation not itself), and keeps the drugs - but the moat is the eroding metabolic franchise, not AI; stock lives and dies on GLP-1 vs Lilly, and AI is an immaterial cheap option.

name: Takeda
verdict_line: Japan's largest pharma; funds the AI-discovery chain (Insilico ~$600m, Iambic up to $1.7bn) and keeps the assets, with one completed proof point (Schrodinger-designed, Takeda-owned zasocitinib through positive Phase III). AI is immaterial to a ~JPY 4.5tn base; the real story is a franchise moat being spent down through a VYVANSE/ENTYVIO patent cliff, so the stock reads fair-to-cheap on the pipeline, not on AI.

name: BioNTech
verdict_line: Clearest EU AI-native drug play by capability (in-house InstaDeep stack) and best-capitalized name in the AI-drug cohort (~EUR 16.8bn cash, a $1.5bn-upfront partnered BNT327 lead), but today's value rests on the pipeline and the balance sheet, not the AI - a real cost-saver, not a proven clinical moat; priced net of cash the pipeline EV is modest, so a fair-to-full pipeline-and-capital-allocation bet dressed in AI clothing.

name: Sophia Genetics
verdict_line: Real asset-light genomics-SaaS with software-grade margins and a small but genuine decentralized data-network moat; not yet a proven compounder - mid-teens constant-currency growth and live cash burn mean the thesis rests on reaching breakeven before dilution.

name: Owkin
verdict_line:
The EU's Tempus-for-pharma with a real, scarce pharma-access / GDPR-federated-data asset, but a moat that rents rather than owns; a ~$1bn 2021 unicorn mark its own carve-outs (Waiv, Bioptimus) and the commoditizing agentic-software layer no longer clearly support - size for pharma-distribution optionality, not a durable software annuity.</verdict_line>
</invoke>

name: Oxford Nanopore
verdict_line: A genuine sole-source nanopore platform monopoly with a real consumable annuity and an AI basecaller welded to the hardware, priced fairly (~5x EV/sales) because the market withholds a software multiple; the moat (~7-10yr of platform IP) is real but the risk is financial - still pre-profit, burning ~GBP 100m/yr against ~GBP 303m cash, with adjusted-EBITDA breakeven only promised for FY27 and self-funding for FY28.

name: United Imaging
verdict_line: Genuine China #1-tier imaging OEM taking share from GE/Siemens/Philips with native AI in the box, but priced ~45-50x forward as a secular compounder when it is a capital-heavy, procurement-cycle-driven equipment maker whose overseas growth engine faces a China-medtech geopolitical cap; good business, demanding expectation, AI is a differentiator not yet a moat.

name: Airdoc (Beijing Airdoc Technology)
verdict_line: Clearest listed pure-play on retinal-image AI screening in China with real regulatory firsts and ~73% gross margins, but a sub-scale (~RMB173m) business whose core screen is commoditizing as rivals win the same NMPA Class III clearance; the re-rate rests on an early diagnostic-therapeutic loop and a thin, cost-cut-driven 2025 turn to profit. Conditional value-capturer at a fair-to-full expectation.

name: Ping An Healthcare (Good Doctor)
verdict_line: Now-profitable China telehealth/AI-triage platform whose moat is the Ping An insurance channel, not its AI - about 60% of revenue is related-party F-end enablement, priced as a fair de-risked small-cap turnaround with no AI premium.

name: WuXi AppTec (2359 / HKEX)
verdict_line: Good, wide-moat, cash-generative picks-and-shovels CRDMO leader (FY2025 continuing-ops +21.4%, TIDES +96%, adj OCF RMB 16.67bn, RMB 58bn backlog) whose AI is an ancillary workflow tool, not the story - but the expectation is un-underwritable: >60% of revenue is US, the BIOSECURE Act is now law and WuXi is on the DOD 1260H list with a live June-2026 federal lawsuit, so the equity is a single binary political bet layered on a strong operating base. Confidence HIGH on facts, LOW on verdict.

name: BeiGene (BeOne Medicines)
verdict_line: Real, cash-generative oncology franchise on a proven discover-develop-commercialize engine, but priced (~68x, ~5x sales) as a diversified global compounder when it is still ~70% one drug (Brukinsa), one year into GAAP profit, and carrying a BIOSECURE geopolitics discount; the "AI-native discovery" label is unsupported and should be dropped from the thesis.

name: Lunit
verdict_line: Korea AI-imaging champion with real global distribution and a 2027 breakeven path, but the cash core is acquired SaaS (Volpara) in a crowded low-pricing-power screening market and the durable moat leg (SCOPE pharma biomarker) is still small, lumpy and not US-cleared; priced full for a software re-rate the mix has not yet proven.

name: Vuno (338220 / KOSDAQ)
verdict_line: Rare breakeven medical-AI name, but a single-product, single-country business (DeepCARS ~74% of revenue) riding a reimbursement exception that hits its permanent test around mid-2026, with US FDA entry delayed; ~60% de-rate leaves it fair-to-cheap on the middle case but event-driven and binary.

name: Sysmex
verdict_line: Profitable ~50%-share hematology leader with a durable reagent-annuity moat, cheap on a China/profit reset; the AI + genomics is honest optionality, not the engine - the study's incumbent-diagnostics control case.

name: Preferred Networks
verdict_line: Rare full-stack AI national champion, but as a healthcare-AI name it is an unpriced option not a thesis: drug discovery is one undisclosed vertical with no owned pipeline, no pharma economics, no recent financials, and no traded stub, priced fair-to-cheap after a deliberate 50%+ down-round on a sovereign-AI silicon bet.

name: Qure.ai
verdict_line: Clearest global-south leader in radiology-image AI - scarce distribution (4,500+ sites, 100+ countries), widest FDA-cleared chest-X-ray set, a WHO-cited TB franchise, capital-light per-scan model - but a small (~$23m), still-private business whose core screen is commoditizing and whose re-rate rests on converting a $1-5 screen plus one marquee pharma deal (AstraZeneca) into a durable higher-value clinical annuity; conditional value-capturer at a fair-to-full expectation.

name: Niramai Health Analytix
verdict_line: Real, clinically validated, FDA-touched radiation-free AI breast screen for the market mammography cannot reach - but a ~$9m-funded, ~74-person company selling a low-ASP screen into grant-funded public-health channels has not shown it converts validation into recurring priced demand; high-conviction on the science, low on the return, and unpriceable from outside (private, redacted).

name: Tempus-China / iCarbonX
verdict_line: China multi-omics data-platform analogue to Tempus in ambition, opposite in outcome: consumer data flywheel never got fuel (~6,000 tests, ~96 loci, <1,000 paying users), CFIUS force-divested the cross-border PatientsLikeMe leg, ~40% staff cut in a 2019-2020 cash crisis, and the ~$1bn+ 2016 unicorn mark is a decade-stale private valuation never re-tested; not a demonstrable value-capturer, and the 2021-2026 record is a disclosure blank.

name: Hims & Hers Health
verdict_line: Good, cash-generative subscription brand with a real but rented consumer moat; the AI/data-flywheel that justifies the premium is still narrative, so the expectation is demanding - fair if the flywheel turns and GLP-1 margins normalize, rich if either fails.

name: Teladoc Health
verdict_line: Scaled, real and cheap at ~0.65x sales, but not a good business today: flat-to-declining revenue, a no-moat D2C half on a marketing treadmill, a shallow enterprise distribution moat eroded by its own visit-based pricing reset, and AI that is operational glue not a defensible product; the multiple fairly prices stagnation, and the equity only works if both segments inflect and cash converts ahead of the 2027 convertible wall.

name: Hinge Health
verdict_line: Good business, real moat - but the moat is enterprise payer distribution and the 3,000-client contract book, not the motion AI, which is a margin-funding feature rivals also have; priced full for durable 25-35% compounding that competition and an unproven engagement-yield ramp can erode.

name: Omada Health
verdict_line: Real evidence-and-distribution moat with an early profitability inflection, but growth rides a GLP-1 drug wave its own channel partners could bundle away and the AI is coaching-efficiency tooling not a cleared model - priced full-not-cheap at ~4x forward sales.

name: Oscar Health
verdict_line: Well-run subscale ACA insurer with genuine AI-driven admin efficiency but no MLR lever and a thin moat, priced full for a durable margin recovery into a subsidy cliff (enhanced PTCs expired 31-Dec-2025, Senate blocked the extension) - the expectation is demanding rather than fair.

name: Function Health
verdict_line: Good brand and a genuinely accumulating data asset, but priced ~$2.5bn (~25x est. run-rate) as a data platform when today it is a fast-growing, thin-margin subscription over a commodity, price-warring lab layer; rich until retention proves out and the AI becomes a real capability.
